sections.h2: Which Onslow office sends and collects the bills?
sections.html:
One office handles the whole job: listing and valuing property, then sending and collecting bills. Its Collections Division covers the county plus Holly Ridge, Jacksonville, North Topsail Beach, Richlands and Swansboro, and it also takes vehicle tax on the sliver of Surf City inside Onslow.

Walk-ins are served at 234 NW Corridor Boulevard in Jacksonville on weekdays, starting at 8 and wrapping up at 5. Extensions on the county's list: 910-989-2200 (Administration), 910-989-2201 (Listings), 910-989-2202 (Collections), 910-989-2204 (Land Records) and 910-455-7431 (Appraisal). Cash and checks work at the counter. For a card or e-check, use the county's online search and pay site, which adds a small convenience charge.

Before you list, call Collections. A parcel may owe both a county charge and a municipal one, and Land Records handles boundary and owner name questions.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Onslow?
sections.html:
Onslow spreads across 762.08 square miles of coastal land. Census QuickFacts shows growth from 177,772 residents (2010) to 204,576 (2020) and an estimated 217,175 for 2025, with 268.4 people per square mile at the 2020 count.

  • Dwellings: 91,470 units shelter 75,265 households, 63.7 percent of them owning (2020 to 2024).
  • Money: owned homes sit around $236,400, rents around $1,265, and household income around $68,148.
  • Moves: 78.7 percent held the same address over a year, so about one resident in five relocated.
  • Military ties: 25,185 veterans live here.
  • New building: 1,372 permits went out in 2025.

Steady movement in and out means payoff and title questions are routine, and a seller gains by contacting the tax office before signing a contract.

sections.h2: What is the billing calendar in Onslow?
sections.html:
The county mails bills in July with a September 1 due date, and its Taxes Due page treats a bill as delinquent once January 5 passes unpaid. Registered vehicles are taxed through the state's combined tax and tag system.

Interest starts January 6 under G.S. 105-360, at 2 percent through February 1 and 0.75 percent monthly afterward. Then G.S. 105-369 lets liens be advertised during March through June.

Bills for 2026 were late. A county notice posted August 18, 2026 said personal property bills would go out the final week of August and real estate notices possibly in early September. The September 1, 2026 due date held, with delinquency after January 5, 2027.

Onslow's reappraisal dated January 1, 2026 was postponed a year, so this year's bills rest on the prior reappraisal's values. The county's revaluation page credits Session Law 2026-8 and Session Law 2026-47, with the new values arriving in 2027.

Under a 2001 resolution Onslow reappraises every four years, starting January 1, 2006, and state law allows counties to shorten its eight year maximum.

  • Your 2026 value should mostly match 2025, with changes only for construction or other alterations as of January 1, 2026.
  • Your bill can still rise, since the tax rate set by the Board of Commissioners and by any city or fire district also drives it.
  • An appeal already filed against the 2026 reappraisal value stays alive, and the outcome applies when that value takes effect in 2027.
  • December 31, 2026 was set as the final day to contest the value in use this year, the delayed reappraisal value, or both.

For the 2027 tax year, the usual appeal deadlines and steps return. For the current rate on your parcel, ask the Tax Office or read the rate in the county's adopted budget, since a rate is only final once the Board of Commissioners adopts it.

sections.h2: How can an Onslow owner challenge a value?
sections.html:
Ask for an informal review first. Formal appeals follow the Machinery Act, and the county's Appeals page notes that the steps differ for land and buildings, personal property and vehicles.

Land and building reviews have to be requested before formal appeals open in spring. Personal property billed yearly and vehicles allow 30 days from the bill date.

Appeal sequence for an Onslow County parcel
StageTiming
Informal reviewBefore spring formal appeals (real estate); 30 days from billing (personal property, vehicles)
County board hearingBoard's first session falls between early April and early May; request a hearing before adjournment
State commissionA written notice due 30 days after the board mails its ruling

The table draws on the county Appeals page, G.S. 105-322 and G.S. 105-290. The delay changed the 2026 calendar, so confirm dates with the Tax Office.

sections.h2: What tax relief can an Onslow homeowner claim?
sections.html:
The county's exemption page points to exclusion and deferment options, and the General Statutes define them. A household may use only one of these three.

  • G.S. 105-277.1 covers owners aged 65 or more, or totally and permanently disabled, whose income is within $38,800 for 2026. It removes half the value of the permanent residence, or $25,000 if that is larger.
  • G.S. 105-277.1C gives disabled veterans a $45,000 exclusion and no age or income test.
  • G.S. 105-277.1B caps tax at 4 percent of income, or 5 percent when income runs above the limit up to $58,200, and defers the rest as a lien.

Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor. January is the intended window, and the assessor must accept it until June 1 ahead of the tax year. A circuit breaker filing renews every year. Since a sale ends the deferral and brings the previous three years of deferred tax due, owners in that program should request the full figure before listing.

Active duty families can read the county's military page, which addresses vehicles, boats and mobile homes. It asks for a current Leave and Earnings Statement at each tag renewal from anyone claiming a different home state.

sections.h2: What should I gather before a sale closes in Onslow County?
sections.html:
A closing goes faster when the tax paperwork is ready before the title company asks. Pull these items together while the house is still being shown.

  • The current bill for every taxing unit on the parcel, including any town that bills separately from the county.
  • A payoff from Collections with a good-through date, and a second one if closing might slip past a month end.
  • Any open appeal, since the county says appeals filed against the delayed 2026 reappraisal value remain pending and will apply when that value takes effect in 2027.
  • Any AV-9 paperwork, if you receive an exclusion or circuit breaker benefit.
  • Land Records contact details for any boundary or owner name mismatch between the deed and the parcel record.

Onslow's Board of Commissioners adopted its FY2027 budget on June 29, according to the Tax Office page. The tax rate comes out of that budget process, so request the rate for your own parcel and skip older bills.

sections.h2: What if the house sells while tax is still owed?
sections.html:
Overdue tax attaches to the parcel as of the listing date, with interest and costs, and a buyer's title search will turn it up. Left alone, the lien can be advertised and foreclosed under G.S. 105-374 or 105-375, and Collections can tell you which route applies.

A private sale puts the price and calendar in your hands. Request a payoff naming every taxing unit, with a good-through date, because interest steps up on January 6 and again after February 1. The seller also pays deed tax of $1 per $500 of price to the register, and G.S. 161-10 sets recording fees. For a vacant, inherited or worn-out house, Cash Home Buyers can quote an as-is price to compare against those costs.

faqs.q: When do Onslow bills fall due?
faqs.a: September 1. The county's Taxes Due page says bills become delinquent when unpaid after January 5 of the next year, and interest begins on January 6 under G.S. 105-360.

faqs.q: Where do I take a payment in Jacksonville?
faqs.a: Take it to 234 NW Corridor Boulevard in Jacksonville. The office opens at 8 on weekdays and closes at 5. Call 910-989-2202 for Collections or 910-989-2200 for Administration.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 Onslow appeal window still open?
faqs.a: The county said appeals could be filed through December 31, 2026, for the value in use this year, the delayed reappraisal value or both. The usual deadlines return for 2027, so call the Tax Office.

faqs.q: Which towns does the Onslow County Tax Office bill for?
faqs.a: The county, plus Holly Ridge, Jacksonville, North Topsail Beach, Richlands and Swansboro. Only vehicle tax is collected for the Onslow portion of Surf City.

faqs.q: Must a seller pay what is owed on the parcel?
faqs.a: Yes, until the balance is paid or paid off. Unpaid tax is a lien from the listing date. Ask Collections for a payoff and have the closing agent settle it at closing.
